title: Worksheet 5: String Indexing
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: Because a string is made up of a sequence of individual characters, each character within a string has a specific position, called an "index," that allows a programmer to access any single character directly. In most programming languages, string indexing starts counting at 0 rather than 1, meaning the very first character in a string is located at index 0, the second character is at index 1, and so on. For example, in the string "Robot", the letter "R" is at index 0, the letter "o" is at index 1, and the final letter "t" is at index 4. Attempting to access an index that does not exist within a string, such as asking for index 10 in a five-letter word, typically causes an error, since there is no character actually stored at that position. String indexing is especially useful for tasks like checking the first letter of a word, reversing a string, or extracting a smaller piece of text from within a longer string.
